title: Dodecanuclear 3d/4f-metal clusters with a ‘Star of David’ topology: single-molecule magnetism and magnetocaloric properties

synthesis.procedure: Under aerobic conditions, solids Co(NO3)2·6H2O (0.09 g, 0.3 mmol) and Gd(NO3)3·6H2O (0.14 g, 0.3 mmol) were added to a stirred colorless MeCN (20 mL) solution of naphthalene-2,3-diol (ndH2; 0.10 g, 0.6 mmol) and NEt3 (84 μL, 0.6 mmol). The green solution was stirred at room temperature for about 10 min, filtered, and the filtrate was diffused with Et2O (40 mL). Slow mixing for 2 days gave gold prismatic crystals, collected by filtration, washed with cold MeCN (2 × 2 mL) and Et2O (2 × 2 mL), and dried in air. The main text describes the same reaction using equimolar M(NO3)2·6H2O and Ln(NO3)3·6H2O with two equivalents each of ndH2 and NEt3 in MeCN/Et2O (yield >65% for the family).
synthesis.vessel_or_method: aerobic MeCN solution with Et2O diffusion
synthesis.workup_and_crystallization: Filtered; Et2O diffusion gave gold prismatic crystals after 2 days, washed with cold MeCN (2 × 2 mL) and Et2O (2 × 2 mL), and dried in air.

properties.summary: Dc susceptibility (2.0–300 K, 0.1 T) is nearly constant from about 70–300 K, consistent with very weak exchange, then falls on cooling; a χMT rise between 10 and 3.5 K is assigned to a ferromagnetic outer Co6 shell plus an antiferromagnetic inner Gd6 core. Magnetization increases toward saturation from 2 to 10 K. Magnetocaloric effect: −ΔSm reaches 12.0R (23.7 J kg−1 K−1) for μ0ΔH = 7 T at 2.7 K, and the magnetic entropy tends toward 15.4R. The lattice contribution has Debye temperature ΘD = 29.6 K. No zero-field ac out-of-phase signal is reported for this analogue.

properties.summary: Dc χMT (2.0–300 K, 0.1 T) is nearly constant from about 70–300 K and decreases rapidly below about 60 K, attributed to antiferromagnetic exchange and/or depopulation of excited MJ states. Magnetization (2–10 K) rises with field but does not saturate, indicating anisotropy and/or low-lying excited states. Zero-field ac studies did not show the frequency-dependent χ'' response reported only for Ni6Dy6 and Zn6Dy6.

Magnetization of the M6Gd6 analogues increases continuously from 2 to 10 K with a trend toward saturation. No zero-field ac out-of-phase signal is reported for this analogue.

synthesis.procedure: Prepared in the same manner as complex 3 (aerobic; ndH2 0.10 g, 0.6 mmol; NEt3 84 μL, 0.6 mmol; Ni(NO3)2·6H2O 0.09 g, 0.3 mmol; MeCN 20 mL; Et2O 40 mL diffusion) but using Dy(NO3)3·6H2O (0.14 g, 0.3 mmol) in place of Gd(NO3)3·6H2O. After 2 days, small green prismatic crystals were collected, washed with cold MeCN (2 × 2 mL) and Et2O (2 × 2 mL), and dried in air. The structure has ten H2O and four MeCN ligands rather than the x = 2, y = 12 solvation of 1–3.

properties.summary: Magnetically a Gd6 system because Zn(II) is diamagnetic. χMT decreases steadily below about 60 K, indicating weak antiferromagnetic Gd···Gd exchange through naphthoxido and μ-nitrate bridges. The Gd(III) spins are weakly correlated; Sm reaches the full 6R ln(8) ≅ 12.5R. The magnetocaloric effect approaches this limit, with −ΔSm = 11.6R (22.8 J kg−1 K−1) at μ0ΔH = 7 T and T = 2.0 K (maximum entropy content 12.5R = 25.1 J kg−1 K−1). Debye temperature ΘD = 29.6 K.

properties.summary: Dc χMT decreases rapidly below about 60 K and magnetization does not saturate. In a 3 G oscillating field and zero dc field, frequency-dependent out-of-phase χ'' tails appear below about 5 K (Fig. 5). The behavior is ascribed mainly to single-ion anisotropy of Dy(III) and is described as slow relaxation typical of high-nuclearity single-molecule magnets. No energy barrier is reported.
